title: 15min reset and manager primers
body:
Purpose: quick, calendarless ritual to capture signal before the 1:1. Mostly a scratchpad — keep short.

15-minute reset ritual (daily/weekly variant)
- 0-2 min: breathing + single sentence about energy level (today: 6/10, low on context).
- 2-6 min: three bullet wins since last sync (quantify where possible).
  - Reduced time-to-offer from 14 -> 11 days (small sample, recruiting pilot).
  - Launched new interview rubric for infra candidates; 3/4 interviewers rated rubric useful.
  - Payroll / benefits FAQ updated; CS tickets down ~8% week-over-week.
- 6-10 min: two friction items that need manager help (one ask per item).
  - Need approval to run one-week hiring blitz budget (+$8k) to close two SWE IC reqs — risk: pipeline drying in EMEA. Ask: prioritize approval this week.
  - Escalation: offboarding docs inconsistent for contractors, causing access delays. Ask: designate SRE contact to speed removals.
- 10-13 min: one career signal / narrative to surface.
  - Signal: owned cross-org interview rubric and rolled to 5 hiring panels -> impact story for promotion case (coaching, execution, outcomes).
- 13-15 min: close with one line ask for 1:1 and a check: what support do you want from me?

Manager 1:1 primer (next sync: 2026-03-04, 30m)
- Topline (1 min): Focused on reducing time-to-hire and tightening contractor offboarding.
- Wins (2-3 bullets):
  - Hiring funnel ships: 12% conversion improvement in targeted mid-funnel after rubric + standardized scorecards (A/B pilot, small n).
  - Admin win: FAQ + payroll note reduced repeat tickets; saved ~3 hours/week for ops lead.
- Asks (3 bullets, concrete):
  1) Approve one-week hiring blitz budget (+$8k) to run targeted outreach and interview slots (metrics expected: add 18 screened candidate slots).
  2) Champion assigning an SRE on contractor offboarding checklist with 24h SLA for access removal.
  3) Backfill one recruiting sourcer headcount (temp contract) — approve request RL-3245 to start hiring requisition.
- Risks/unknowns: EMEA interviewers overloaded in April -> may delay hires; metric: 20% more no-shows historically during Q2 holidays.
- One coaching ask for manager: short debrief after candidate panel for harder feedback loops (10 min cadence).

Evidence snippets (copy into promotion packet or quarterly review)
- Feb 02 — Interview rubric rollout deck (internal): 5-panel pilot feedback; average rubric usefulness 4.1/5. Link: RL-3245.
- Feb 18 — Hiring velocity chart: time-to-offer dropped by 3 days vs baseline for roles using standardized scorecards. (note: small sample n=11).
- Mar 01 — Payroll FAQ update: decreased repeat tickets by 8% week-over-week (ops ticketing).
- Anecdote: Candidate A cited 'clarity of interview expectations' as reason to accept. Good qualitative evidence.

Career signal + 90-day asks (scripted)
- Narrative: "Built scalable hiring patterns: created rubric -> trained panels -> measurably improved conversion and reduced friction."
- 90d asks (concise):
  1) Consider me for L4 exploratory project lead on hiring infra (I will draft scope by 3/20).
  2) Support to present hiring rubric results in Q2 all-hands (ask: 15 min slot).
  3) Clear feedback on areas to strengthen (decision-making, up-level comms) — request two explicit examples.

Micro experiments (two-week sprints)
- Experiment A: calendar-blocked "panel debrief" 10m after each panel for 2 weeks; measure interview feedback quality (pre/post checklist completeness). Success = checklist completeness + avg inter-rater SD decreases.
- Experiment B: small-scope sourcer blitz (contract) to test incremental screened pipeline; track screened->onsite conversion. Stop rule: cost per hire > $18k or no lift in screened volume after week 1.

Loose notes / open questions (notes to self)
- Do we have hiring data permission to share in all-hands? Check with legal.
- How to quantify coaching impact objectively? possible metric: interview score variance pre/post coaching.
- Followup: sync with Marcus next Wed re: EMEA interviewer capacity.
- TODOs: draft hiring-blitz one-pager (due 2026-03-02), prepare 2 slides for manager on rubric outcomes.

Quick heuristics (for manager conversations)
- Always lead with impact and one concrete ask.
- Frame requests as tradeoffs (cost, time, risk).
- Bring 1-2 pieces of evidence; if unavailable, state plan to deliver evidence in 48h.

End notes: keep this <1 page in my head — king of micro-ops. If manager wants deeper dive, use linked artifacts above.

[Note to self: copy relevant bullets to quarterly-review packet by Mar 10 — file: reviews/2026-Q1/amir-review-draft (confluence)]
